props.title: Run of show
props.description: Three worked run-of-show templates with the band's rows filled in: a corporate gala, a wedding, and a holiday party. Set times, break placement, volume steps and who cues each moment.

props.html:
Run of show

Three run of show templates, already timed.

Most run-of-show documents carry the band as one row that says band plays, and the detail gets filled in during the week of the event, by email, at speed. Here's that detail already worked out for the three kinds of night we see most. Take them, change the times, delete what doesn't apply.
props._notes:
Run of show templates. The most useful thing on the site for a planner
     who has not hired us: it is work they have to do anyway, done. The band
     rows are the ones normally left as "band plays" until the week of.

props.html:
How to read these

The cue column is the one worth settling before the day. Every moment in an evening belongs to somebody, and what usually goes wrong is two people each assuming the other was going to nod at the band, or nobody knowing who decides the speeches are running long.

Agree the cue column at sound check with the person holding the master document. Our bandleader takes their cues from that one person.

A corporate gala

Four hundred guests, a quartet with a DJ, an 11:30pm curfew. This is the way most awards dinners and fundraisers run.

Two of those rows are worth a second look. The 7:00pm call to dinner is the surest way to move four hundred people from a bar into a seated dinner, and the band plays them in. The 9:15pm changeover matters because a quartet can't get from a dinner setup to a dance setup silently, so the DJ covers that gap.

A wedding, ceremony through late night

A hundred and eighty guests, one venue, a duo for the ceremony and a quartet for the floor. The whole night is booked as one contract.

The row people move most often is 6:45pm. A first dance immediately after the entrances, before anyone has picked up a fork, keeps the whole crowd watching. Held back until after dinner it competes with coffee, and half the guests are outside.

A company holiday party

Two hundred staff, a quartet, a hotel ballroom, an early hard stop. It's shorter and looser, and it's the one where the program is smallest and the dance floor matters most.

The row to watch on this night is 8:00pm. Remarks at a holiday party start late, run long, and land on a crowd that has been drinking since doors opened. Put a hard finish on them in the document, give it to whoever is speaking in advance, and put the band back up on time regardless.

If the program wants a louder set, live band karaoke is its own line on the quote.
